title: Common graphics.h functions

visuals.title: Line, rectangle, circle, ellipse and arc, each with its own colour
Background colour and filling closed shapes
Exam drawing: a traffic light with text

goal: After this you can pick the right graphics.h function for each shape, set colours in the correct order, fill a closed shape and write text on the graphics screen.
warmup: Think of a painter making a signboard for a shop in the bazaar. He first picks the brush colour, then draws the outline, then fills it with paint. If he paints first and picks the colour afterwards, the sign comes out wrong. Graphics programs work the same way: choose the colour, then draw.
definition: graphics.h gives you ready-made functions to draw on the screen: one function per kind of shape (line, rectangle, circle, ellipse, arc), functions to choose colours, and functions to fill and write text. You call initgraph first to switch the screen into graphics mode and closegraph last. graphics.h is not standard C++. It runs only on a lab PC with Turbo C++ (DOSBox) or Code::Blocks/Dev-C++ plus the WinBGIm library, so the in-page compiler cannot run these programs. The canvas on this page is a simulation that draws what the same calls would draw.
howItWorks: Every program has the same frame: initgraph at the start, drawing in the middle, getch to wait for a key, closegraph at the end. In the middle follow one rule: SET the colour BEFORE the shape that should use it, because setcolor only affects shapes drawn after it. Colours are named constants such as RED, GREEN, YELLOW and WHITE (really small numbers, but use the names). To colour the inside of a shape, call setfillstyle(SOLID_FILL, colour) and then floodfill(x, y, border) with a point INSIDE the shape; the third argument must be the colour of the outline, and the outline must be CLOSED, otherwise the colour leaks out and floods the whole screen. Angles for ellipse and arc are in degrees (0 to 360).
syntax:
int gd = DETECT, gm;                      // DETECT = choose the driver automatically
initgraph(&gd, &gm, (char*)"");          // graphics mode ON (path is "" with WinBGIm)

setbkcolor(BLUE);  cleardevice();         // background colour, then clear to show it
setcolor(YELLOW);                         // colour for the NEXT shapes
line(x1, y1, x2, y2);                     // straight line
rectangle(left, top, right, bottom);      // outline
circle(x, y, radius);                     // centre (x, y)
ellipse(x, y, 0, 360, xr, yr);            // full ellipse (0 to 360 degrees)
arc(x, y, 0, 180, r);                     // half circle
setfillstyle(SOLID_FILL, RED);            // pattern and colour of the fill
floodfill(x, y, YELLOW);                  // (x, y) INSIDE; YELLOW = outline colour
outtextxy(x, y, (char*)"Hello");         // text starting at (x, y)
delay(500);                               // pause 500 ms
getch();                                  // wait for a key
closegraph();                             // graphics mode OFF

Set colour LIGHTRED, draw an arc (0 to 180 degrees)

Wait for a key, then close graphics

mistakes.wrong:
// meant to be 100 pixels ABOVE the centre of the screen
circle(320, 340, 30);
mistakes.error: No compiler error. The circle appears BELOW the centre because y grows downwards.
No compiler error. The window may close at once, and graphics memory is not released; always finish with getch() and closegraph().
No compiler error, but graphics mode is not on yet, so the circle is not shown or the program stops with a graphics error. initgraph must come first.
No compiler error. The circle is drawn in the OLD colour; setcolor only affects shapes drawn after it.
No compiler error. The outline has gaps, so the paint leaks out and can colour the whole screen. Fill only closed shapes.

examTips: Learn the frame by heart: include graphics.h, DETECT, initgraph, drawing, getch, closegraph.
Write setcolor BEFORE each shape. A typical exam trap is a colour set after the shape.
floodfill needs a point INSIDE a CLOSED shape and the border colour equal to the outline colour.
Know the argument orders: line(x1,y1,x2,y2), rectangle(left,top,right,bottom), circle(x,y,r), ellipse(x,y,start,end,xr,yr), arc(x,y,start,end,r).
Say that graphics.h is not standard C++ and needs Turbo C++ or WinBGIm.
romanSummary: Har graphics program mein pehle initgraph, phir drawing, phir getch aur aakhir mein closegraph likhte hain.
Shape se PEHLE setcolor likhein, kyun ke setcolor sirf baad mein bani shapes par asar karta hai.
line, rectangle, circle, ellipse aur arc se shapes bante hain. Angle degrees mein hota hai.
Shape ko bharne ke liye setfillstyle aur floodfill, magar shape BAND honi chahiye aur border ka colour wohi ho jo outline ka hai.
outtextxy se text likhte hain, cleardevice screen saaf karta hai, delay thori der rukta hai.

practice.prompt: Which function switches the screen into graphics mode?
practice.hint: It is the first graphics call.
practice.explanation: initgraph(&gd, &gm, path) turns graphics mode on; closegraph turns it off.

practice.prompt: What does DETECT mean in int gd = DETECT?
practice.hint: It is a value for the driver variable.
practice.explanation: With DETECT, initgraph finds the best graphics driver and mode for the computer.

practice.hint: Which function chooses the drawing colour?
practice.explanation: setcolor(RED) comes BEFORE the shape it should colour.

practice.prompt: Which call draws a rectangle whose top-left corner is (50, 100) and bottom-right corner is (250, 200)?

practice.explanation: setcolor only affects shapes drawn after it, so it must come first.
Only three sides are drawn, so the shape is open and the paint leaks. A closed rectangle (all four sides) keeps the fill inside.

practice.prompt: Write a graphics program that draws a yellow circle with centre (320, 240) and radius 80, fills it with red, and then writes the text SUN at (300, 350).
practice.hint: Colour, circle, fill style, floodfill, text.
practice.explanation: The border colour in floodfill (YELLOW) equals the circle outline colour. The program runs on a lab PC with graphics.h; the page only simulates it.

quiz.prompt: Which call must be the LAST graphics call in a program?
quiz.explanation: closegraph returns to text mode and frees memory.

quiz.prompt: When should setcolor(RED) be written to colour a circle red?
quiz.explanation: setcolor affects shapes drawn after it.

quiz.prompt: floodfill(x, y, border) fills correctly only when the shape is...
options: closed and (x, y) is inside it
quiz.answer: closed and (x, y) is inside it
quiz.hint: What happens if paint can leak?
quiz.explanation: An open outline lets the colour escape.

quiz.prompt: What are the angles in arc(x, y, 0, 180, r) measured in?
Which call writes the text Hi with its top-left corner at (10, 20)?
quiz.hint: x, y first, then the text.
quiz.explanation: outtextxy(x, y, text) draws text at a graphics position; cout prints in the console, not on the graphics screen.
